name: frugally-deep
listed_description: Header-only library for using Keras models in C++.
reason: No win over TensorFlow in any numbers found. Current README and FAQ (opened) give only qualitative claims ('quite fast on one CPU core'; FAQ: 'with single 2D convolutions ... depending on the dimensions even faster than TensorFlow', no numbers) and list 'roughly 2, 4, 10 and 100 times slower than Python' as troubleshooting cases (no GPU, one core, no kernel fusion). test/Dockerfile and test/applications_performance.cpp print timings but no results are published. A fork copy of an older README (https://github.com/dashpritam/frugally-deep) has a single-core Intel Core i5-6600, GCC 7.1 g++ -O3 -march=native, GPU disabled table in which Keras + TF is faster on all 17 models (e.g. DenseNet121 0.11 s vs 0.25 s, MobileNet 0.06 s vs 0.15 s, VGG16 0.40 s vs 0.56 s, NASNetLarge 1.31 s vs 4.03 s). A third-party JIT-compiler paper (arXiv 1906.05737, seen only in search snippet) reports it slower than TensorFlow Lite on an Atom E3845. Could be recorded as a not-faster entry if wanted. MIT, 1.1k stars.

name: Genann
listed_description: Simple neural network library in C.
reason: Directional claim only: README feature list says 'Fast and thread-safe' with no numbers and no comparison against any library; it mentions tinn, FANN and Lightweight Neural Network only as alternatives. No benchmark found in the repo or by search. zlib, 2.3k stars.

name: Kaldi
reason: No numeric comparison against TensorFlow, PyTorch or any recognizable external baseline. README and repo page have no speed claims. Only speed numbers found (search snippets, pages not opened because kaldi-asr.org is not reachable here) are Kaldi against its own older setups: docs chain.html says chain (LF-MMI) models decode about 3x faster than conventional DNN-HMMs, and a CTU Prague thesis reports an LSTM-TDNN chain model about 9x faster than standard nnet3. The baseline is Kaldi itself, so no record. 15.5k stars.

name: luacxx
listed_description: C++11 API for creating Lua bindings.
reason: No numbers anywhere. README only lists 'Low-overhead userdata and conversion support' as a focus and says it works with the Lua C API rather than hiding it. Not among the 15 binding libraries in ThePhD/lua-bindings-shootout (opened on github.com; baseline there is plain C Lua 5.3.4) and not found in the sol2 benchmark material surfaced by search. MIT, 164 stars, last commit 2026-03-13.

name: MetaCall
listed_description: Cross-platform Polyglot Runtime which supports NodeJS, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, C#, Wasm, Java, Cobol and more
reason: No comparison against V8, SpiderMonkey or any native runtime. README and docs make no speed claims. The repo's source/benchmarks (Google Benchmark: metacall_py_call_bench, metacall_node_call_bench, metacall_cs_call_bench, metacall_rb_call_bench, py_init_bench, log_bench, set_bench) only time MetaCall's own cross-language call and init paths for regression tracking; the metacall_py_c_api_bench 'native Python C API' case has an empty timed loop. Published results are on metacall.github.io/core/bench/, which is blocked here, but they come from those same self-only benchmarks. Apache-2.0, 1.8k stars.

name: MiniScript
listed_description: scripting language modern, elegant, easy to learn, and easy to embed in your own C# or C++ projects.
reason: No speed claims or numbers found. The GitHub repo page and README (opened) have no performance statement or comparison with Lua, Python or others; miniscript.org does not resolve from this environment; a WebSearch for MiniScript benchmarks returned nothing specific. MIT, 388 stars.
